searchText: > Is it easier than requesting the txHash? I understand it is potentially more flexible but in practice, seems a lot cheaper (in terms of coreDev time and potentially gas) to simply have an opcode to export all aspects of the transaction, including the txHash. You mean just the *current* transaction hash here, right? The main risk I see with that is that it would make it more difficult for us to change transaction formats around eg. there's been a push recently to try to move toward SSZ I do mean the current transaction. Today, out of the current transaction, I can get - gas price - to - value in wei - data I cannot get - nonce - gas limit - ecdsaV - ecdsaR - txHash At the exception of gas limit, those information should remain in any new version. Even in the case of nonce being removed, one could simply set the returning value to -1 to address this edge caze. <@!619138323776012307> Everything you listed is part of a transaction. If your tool isn't giving it to you that is a problem with your tool I think. My point is that - nonce - ecdsaV - ecdsaR - txHash will be part of any new version of transaction structure and should be accessible to the EVM. Today, every user refers to the transaction by its txHash. So, if I want to condition something on a transaction, the natural identifier is the txHash Ah, I see. You want all that info available from within the EVM. Yes. Vitalik point is that it could make migration to a new transaction format harder to which I agree. This is why access gas limit is contentious. But we will always have a signature and we will always have a txHash. my concern is basically, imagine we move to SSZ serialization then the hash of a tx would be different, even if the contents are the same But that's not an issue :) I don't want to compute the txHash in the EVM, I just wish to access the txHash within the EVM.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: > Is it easier than requesting the txHash? I understand it is potentially more flexible but in practice, seems a lot cheaper (in terms of coreDev time and potentially gas) to simply have an opcode to export all aspects of the transaction, including the txHash.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: You mean just the *current* transaction hash here, right?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: The main risk I see with that is that it would make it more difficult for us to change transaction formats around

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: eg. there's been a push recently to try to move toward SSZ

excerpts.author: guthl_starkware
excerpts.content:
I do mean the current transaction. 
Today, out of the current transaction, I can get 
- gas price
- to
- value in wei
- data
I cannot get 
- nonce
- gas limit
- ecdsaV
- ecdsaR
- txHash

At the exception of gas limit, those information should remain in any new version. 
Even in the case of nonce being removed, one could simply set the returning value to -1 to address this edge caze.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: <@!619138323776012307> Everything you listed is part of a transaction.  If your tool isn't giving it to you that is a problem with your tool I think.

excerpts.author: guthl_starkware
excerpts.content:
My point is that 
- nonce
- ecdsaV
- ecdsaR
- txHash
will be part of any new version of transaction structure and should be accessible to the EVM.
Today, every user refers to the transaction by its txHash. So, if I want to condition something on a transaction, the natural identifier is the txHash

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Ah, I see.  You want all that info available from within the EVM.

excerpts.author: guthl_starkware
excerpts.content:
Yes. Vitalik point is that it could make migration to a new transaction format harder to which I agree. This is why access gas limit is contentious.
But we will always have a signature and we will always have a txHash.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: my concern is basically, imagine we move to SSZ serialization

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: then the hash of a tx would be different, even if the contents are the same

excerpts.author: guthl_starkware
excerpts.content:
But that's not an issue :)
I don't want to compute the txHash in the EVM, I just wish to access the txHash within the EVM.
